entry.title: Successful company policies
entry.content:
Introduction

This post introduces critical policies to creating a successful business. They are:

  • Feedback Mechanism
  • Core company culture
  • Team bonding
  • Democratic congress (民主会议)

Feedback Mechanism

At Quant-Speed, we have a 谈薪日 at the beginning of every month. The manager and and the employee will be in a private, safe and comfortable room discussing:

  • What the employee thinks their salary should be
  • The employee will reflect on:
    • what work they did well/bad on
    • comment on who they liked best/done the best work
    • what the manager did that is good/bad
  • The manager provide analysis on the employee’s work, and suggestions for improvements

Core Company Values (Most critical)

Countries are birthed from simple and abstract core values - America for freedomn, China for the people (ref. Sapien by Yuval Noah). In detail, the slogan for the two contries are:

  • Freedom!
  • 为人民服务！

respectively. Notably, the ideas are simple and evoke a sense of grandure. This is a powerful tool to bind individuals towards a common goal.

At Quantum-Speed, we follow those two principals and come up with two core values:

  • 世界一流工程师
  • 进入人类AI时代

Observe that these ideas are simple and grandure. I think one of the reason the ideas are so effective is because they leave a huge room for Imagination.

Team bonding

Of course, no body will believe in those core values if they are simply reverberated over and over again. Team bonding is a place where we reinforce those ideas by practicing those ideas. Most critically, to make everyone say those slogans so they believe in them

Democratic congress

The manager writes a speech to reinforce the core values.

A reference speech is a speech from Alexander the great before the soldiers head into battle. In the prior night before the battle, Alexander would consult his commanders on the names of those with significant contribution in the wars. On the day of the battle, Alexander, riding on horse back, would ride infront of the soldier as if randomly and call him out by name and state the soldier’s contribution giving an illusion that he knows all the soldiers by their personal names. He would use that soldier’s contribution as example for his Core Values.

An example I could use is to comment Shuang’s improvement and link it back to that he is moving towards 世界一流工程师 one step at a time. Haha, feels like Gan is going to critisize me for this shallow of an example.

**Update - the main activity here is criticizing yourself and others since on normal work days, these opportunities are extremely rare. Topics are not limit to:

  • work progress
  • communications

entry.title: Setup SSL for HTTPS
entry.content:
Introduction

This is a tutorial on how to setup the ssl certification to enable https for a website

Step1 - Setup DNS Forwarding

Add direct forwarding to DNS. Here we use agent as example. We add a subdomain to quant-speed.com so the link is agent.quant-speed.com.

The DNS panel for configuration (Aliyun example).

Step2 - Initial nginx setup

After nginx installation, in the directory /etc/nginx/conf.d, create agent.quant-speed.com.conf with

server {
    listen 80;                                  # 80 is http port
    server_name agent.quant-speed.com;          # target url

    # Allow Let's Encrypt to verify domain ownership
    location ^~ /.well-known/acme-challenge/ {
        root /var/www/letsencrypt;  # webroot directory for verification
        try_files $uri =404;
    }

    # Proxy other requests to backend service
    location / {
        proxy_pass http://localhost:8589;       # port to forward to
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
    }
}

check if the config is correct with nginx -t
restart to check if it works sudo systemctl restart nginx

Step3 - Setup SSL

Install acme.sh

git clone https://github.com/acmesh-official/acme.sh.git
cd ./acme.sh
./acme.sh --install -m my@example.com

Make a directory for acme to challenge

# Create directory and set owner to www-data (recommended)
sudo mkdir -p /var/www/letsencrypt
sudo chown -R www-data:www-data /var/www/letsencrypt
sudo chmod -R 755 /var/www/letsencrypt

Create directory for SSL certificates

sudo mkdir -p /etc/nginx/tls/agent

Apply for the SSL

# change `agent.quant-speed.com` to target url
# After installation, acme.sh is typically at ~/.acme.sh/acme.sh
~/.acme.sh/acme.sh --issue -d agent.quant-speed.com --webroot /var/www/letsencrypt

It is a success if you see:

/gT2UalfrnC37aJu0bHy1BWQgGy2uuI2KDAjBgNVHREEHDAaghh4aWFvdGFpLnRh
bmdsZWR1cC1haS5jb20wCgYIKoZIzj0EAwMDaQAwZgIxAP/pcT9+4yh/IVfYoZ66
tDCOA8Pz/XfQCDTfhHb4kEpgToJSisFsT13n2jMvxCj3bQIxAM/O1CA0HAB8LbWS
AfBade7OOyXxEsAwCIzairGq2jMSzZGhiTT3vvyZ4DuV/9dd+g==
-----END CERTIFICATE-----

Install the key. Critical Notes

  • update agent.quant-speed.com to target url
  • that agent in --fullchain-file
~/.acme.sh/acme.sh --install-cert -d agent.quant-speed.com \
  --key-file /etc/nginx/tls/agent/key.pem \
  --fullchain-file /etc/nginx/tls/agent/cert.pem \
  --reloadcmd "service nginx force-reload"
sudo chown www-data:www-data /etc/nginx/tls/agent/*.pem
sudo chmod 600 /etc/nginx/tls/agent/*.pem  # Ensure only owner can read/write

Step4 - Update config with SSL

Update /etc/nginx/conf.d/agent.quant-speed.com.conf to redirect HTTP to HTTPS and add HTTPS server block:

# HTTP server block - redirects to HTTPS except for Let's Encrypt verification
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name agent.quant-speed.com;
    
    # Allow Let's Encrypt to verify domain ownership (needed for renewals)
    location ^~ /.well-known/acme-challenge/ {
        root /var/www/letsencrypt;
        try_files $uri =404;
    }
    
    # Redirect all other HTTP traffic to HTTPS
    location / {
        return 301 https://$server_name$request_uri;
    }
}

# HTTPS server block
server {
    listen 443 ssl http2;                                   # HTTPS 
    server_name agent.quant-speed.com;                      # update to target url

    # SSL certificate paths
    ssl_certificate     /etc/nginx/tls/agent/cert.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/nginx/tls/agent/key.pem;

    # Proxy configuration (same as HTTP block)
    location / {
        proxy_pass http://localhost:8589;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
    }
}

check if the config is correct with nginx -t
restart to check if it works sudo systemctl restart nginx

YOU ARE DONE!

entry.title: Bayer meeting recollection
entry.content:
Introduction

A business meeting is no different from a political one. This post is a recollection of our meeting at Bayer. It details:

  • How different interest groups reacts to our arrival - bringing AI to Bayer.
  • How we should approach different interest groups to establish further deals
  • The different conversational and persuation skills used

Background

At Kunming, Bayer is digitizing and introducing AI via Dify into their manufacturing pipeline. We were invited as technical consultants to advice them on their AI approaches. When we entered the meeting room, our sitting location are as below.

The basic sitting of our the meeting room. Gan sits face to face with the manager. There are two interest groups in this meeting - office camp and the factory camp. The office camp focuses on data analysis and visualization using PowerBI. The factory camp focuses on the manuefacturing process. We have a mole in the office camp.

We were invited to discuss details about how to train their employees to use Dify. But, our hidden main goal is to influence Bayer to choose us as, possibly, their AI supplier.

Identifying interest groups and motivations

It is of utmost importance to identify how many camps are in the room and what their motivations to direct us on how to navigate the discussion to our goal. There are three notable camps in the room:

  • 深总(For bervity, Mr.Shen) - the head of Bayer at Kunming
  • The factory camp
  • The office camp

Motivation Analysis

Mr.Shen

We analyze Mr.Shen from 2 aspects - Age and position in the company. He is in is late 40s and at the top position in Kunming. Due to his age, he is at his late stage of his career. He is just at a point in his age that he can climb one more step up the corporate ladder before retirement. He needs a notible achievement(政绩) to justify his promotion. Hence he is very motivated to introduce AI into Bayer. He is a strong supporting camp.

The German Superior - he is one level above Mr.Shen. We had intel that he was in Kunming, but why isn’t he there? Because Mr.Shen wants to:

  • make sure we can actually do work
  • we are His People when we meet Mr.Shen to bolster his achievement

The Office Camp

We analyze the office camp from the nature of their work. Part of their task involves data visualization via powerBI - easily replacible by AI today. Hence, they are threatened by our arrival. How the head of the department questions our data visualization further corroborates our hypothesis. He attempts to find all avenues of flaws in our demonstrations.

Mr.Shen Notes Mr.Shen is extremely smart. When the office head critisize the AI visualizations, Mr. Shen observes that the office head was threatened and IMMEDATELY comforts him by saying: “when we move forward with the visualization ai-fication, you’ll be in charge of the change”. GENIUS!

Update Note - After dinner with our mole, the office head appears to be a smart scholar. Trained as a researcher myself, I see his need to absolutely confirm that there is an advantage in switching to AI before implementation - local optima are rare.

So, it is hard to determine at this point. But, we will stick to the conclusion that this is an opposing camp.

The Factory Camp

Similar to the office camp, we analyze them by the nature of their work. Early on the meeting, we saw excitement when we mentioned computer vision (CV). This implies that they focus on efficiency and are open to introduce AI related technology to help them. Hence when we mentioned using multi-modal AI to aid them, they were extremely excited. Hence, this is a strong support camp.

Our Moves

Now that the hidden motivation of all the players are revealed. How we persuade them in future meetings is clear. We will align ourselves strongly with both Mr.Shen and the factory camp and use our mole from the office camp to change the office camp’s mind.

On Answering Questions

Answer the actual need of the quetioner and not the question asked. In the beginning of the meeting, Mr.Shen intelligently verbalize all his concerns. One of which is whether they should use Dify or not. Our opinion is that they should not because Dify is too clunky. We stopped using it some months ago.

With deeper observation, the question on Dify usage is actually “whether Dify will actually solve their existing problem”. Gan was observant to realize this, so he did not answer this question at all but instead expand on the capability of AI instead - leading into a small discussion on multi-modal AI.

Personal Note - I think this is actually the fault of the questioner’s capability to ask questions as he was incapable of identifying the most valuable piece of information he needs for quality decision making.

My Blunder

I made a mistake of attempting Mr.Shen, the LEADER, infront of his underlings. Doing so damages his reputation. Further, proving him wrong does not prove us better than those at Bayer - so correcting him is a USELESS and HARMFUL action.

Early on the meeting, Mr.Shen mentioned that AI was capable of solving unsolved math problems. That was incorrect as I recall that progress were made to those math problems in 1920s. It was a case of test data leakage. As I just started to correct him, he shuts me and states that math is not of a concern - at the same time, comforting me that I’m not entirely wrong to respect my expertise. Doing so saves his face and respecting my dignity at the same time. Mr.Shen is so so brilliant.

After Note

It was a brilliant meeting in everyway. After the meeting, Mr.Shen personally returned to the meeting room and took our panflet. It is a great sign. We will attempt to analyze their pain point and come up with a demo by the end of the Dify training. It is quite hopeful that we can achieve some sort of collaboration.

entry.title: Siggraph Asia 2025 Overview
entry.content:
Things remembered from SIGGRAPH ASIA 2025

Papers

  • Physics-based Motion Imitation with adversarial differential discriminator
    • Manual tuning is required to balance the different rewards in a RL system for the agent to learn desirable motion. They used a discriminator instead. So the loss becomse $-\log(1-D(\Delta r))$ where $\Delta r$ is the error (assuming supervised learning). True examples would be a zero vector compared to the error vector.
  • Temporally Smooth Mesh Extraction for Procedural Scenes with Long-Range Camera Trajectories using Spacetime Octrees
    • cool tree split in time dimension for different resolution of render from occupancy function
  • ASIA: Adaptive 3D Segmentation using Fiew Image Annotations
    • Given image with desired segmentation, learn some correlation embedding in a diffusion model for those regions. Use the embeddings to classify renders of the mesh from different view. Maintain multi-view consistency by voting and consensus between views
  • Underwater Optical Backscatter Communication using Acousto-Optic Beam Steering
    • Problem formulation: When under water, WIFI, Radio don’t work. Using lazer to communicate for the underwater rover is too engergy intensive + only sending Kb level of data
    • proposed solution: Attatch the lazer on the ship on the surface instead. Attach a mirror on the underwater rover. Play sound onto the reflected light to transmit information back. Information on Kb level
  • MVP4D: Multi-View Portrait Video Diffusion for Animatable 4D Avatars
    • Given a single human portrain image, estimate a 3dmm parameter as reference. From that reference, generate facial animations. Yank the animations into a diffusion model and yank some noise in. Voila, a simple dataset of the identity. Yank that to a 4D 3dmm, and voila 3d animatable human
  • GS-RoadPatching: Inpainting Gaussians VIA 3D Searching And Placing for Driving Scenes.
    • Inspired by patch inpainting techniques, for missing patches of gaussians, say for a road, find regions of gaussians of simular properties and fill it in. Due to view dependence of retrieved patch, the stiched patch does not look appealing. So, they use the source view of the retrieved patch as psuedo ground truth and train the stiched path to look like the source patch.
  • WireDrum: An Interpersonal and Multimodal Skill-Sharing System for an Augmented Drumming Experience
    • Attach electric node on student, when the teacher does a drumm hitting action. Shocks the student’s muscle to do the same thing
  • Hapticus: A Haptic Customization tool for effective Physical Skill Learning
    • Introduced 2 approaches: 1) electric shock 2) a exoskeleton that will make the finger press on piano key. More experienced learner prefer electric shocks
  • Spectral prefiltering of Neural networks:
    • apply kernal to images learned as neural networks
    • consider a image encoded as a MLP with positional encoding, applying a kernal, eg. a bandpass filter, is equivalent to applying the a filter in the fourier space. By generating different gaussian filters and train, the MLP generalize and learns formulations of different filters
  • Neural Image Abstraction Using Long Smoothing B-splines
    • Better formulated initialization compared to random init
    • use B-splines for better optimization of stroke positions
  • QMF-BLEND: Quantized Matrix Factorization for Efficient Blendshape Compression (my favourite)
    • Prelim: A blendshape is a reference head mesh $R$ with $\Delta r$ that describe possible morphing (similar to orthogonal basis). So, $R + W\Delta r$ describes all possible expression
    • Method notable ideas:
      • use matrix factorization to sparcify $\Delta r$ for storage. Adam is used for the factorization because the zeroing of the elements in the matrix is equivalent to introducing noise. Adam is built specifically for this scenerio.
      • add a laplacian to ensure smoothness. Specifically, the laplacian is on the error of the factorization and not the factorization. If applied on the factorization, facial wrinkles will be removed
      • find locations with surface difformations and push non-zero values to those areas by importance weighting.
      • Finally, quantize
  • Gaussian See, Gaussian Do: Semantic 3D Motion Transfer from Multiview Video:
    • Define object centric embeddings based on angles. For different angles use slerp interpolation between the embeddings and to find the inverted motion embedding
    • Condition on a reference identity target image and the motion embeddings to obtain a video of the target identity doing the source motion
    • Yank that onto a gaussian. Voila!
  • Fast and stable control of coupled solid-fluid dynamic systems
    • cool ball flying. Looks really cool
  • HR $\text{M}^2$ Avatar: High-Fidelity Real-Time Mobile Avatars from Monocular Phone scans$
    • 3D representation of Gaussian that runs on phones

Camera control video-gen papers

  • Context As Memory: Scene-Consistent Interactive Long Video Generation with memory retrieval
    • RAG based retrieval of seen latents based on previous camera trajectory. Makes video generators consistent
  • CamCloneMaster: Enabling Reference-based camera control for Video Generation
    • Clones reference camera motion to target scene

HCI papers (Funny; Posters only)

  • GPStroke: A walking Promotion Method using GPS Art with Multiple walking Paths
    • Walk paths such that they look like images. Encourage walking
  • Neck-Warn Tactile Choker
    • A neck chocker with different vibrators. Example usage: When following map directions, vibration tells direction so no need to look at phone
  • Towards wearable-free Exergame for Orthostatic Dyregulation: Improving Motion Detection with Smartphone-Only Calibration
    • Game that doesn’t use hand to play, use legs instead to fix some issues
  • Acoustic form: Enhancing the design process for assistive earwear jewlry via material-centric computational sound analysis
    • Stigma towards assistive hearing devices. Here, they make the device looks like jewlery so people will wear them by evaluating geometry and material choice before

Manufacture papers

  • Curve-Based Slicer for Multi-Axis DLP
    • water based with rotating arm. The arm rotation removes the need for support structures
  • INF-3DP: Implicit Neural Fields for Collision-Free multi-axis 3D printing
    • Finds a rotating arm trajectory to 3D print objects without contact
  • Can Any Model Be Frabricated? Inverse Operation Based Planning for Hybrid Additive-Subtractive Manufacturing
    • First attempt at printing by adding and subtracting with a voxel based planning approach

Demos:

  • Enhanced Touch: Delivering vibrotile and Thermal feedback without fingerpad contact
    • Different vibrations for touching of different materials on ipad.
    • On water: Vibration + cold
    • On warm water: Vibration + warm
  • Pro’s Eyes: A Wearable system for synchronous and asynchronous observational pattern learning:
    • a glasses that have recordings of expert. When a user wears the glasses, it will replay the eye movement. Examples:
      • replay the eye movement of a arts professor of how he/she observe the art
      • replay eye movement of a police officer looking for suspect in a crowd

Memorable talk

  • Base CEO - on nezha2
    • Chinese directors like big cinematic pieces, the US focus more on characters
    • China market is the number for animated films. Nezha’s local box office beats all other areas combined

Memorable company:

  • Unicus:
    • Image $\to$ 3d lego pieces. Print the lego and sells it.

entry.title: Joining Tangled Up
entry.content:
The Journey

It all started with a random wechat post from Jeremy. I have noticed his posts from time to time starting from two/three years ago. The initial posts were on teaching how people use ChatGPT. It slowly evolved to case competitions. They all looked like scams. But given that he is the madman I have known him for, I decided to visit.

We had an unforgettable talk the night I visited. He is still as crazy as I known him for. I was shocked that he was able to create such an interesting product, a simple hardware capable of using MCP and speaking in multiple Chinese dialect, in a span of a year-ish. I realized how herculean such a task was given that he did not know how to solder nor code a year ago.

The company culture also shocked me. They were taking a salary of less than 600USD per month and were willing to work 12+hrs per day. Their eyes had dreams. Their energy was unbelievable. I was left with the question: “what kind of leadership and management can create such a culture?”

I was dejected and depressed at the time due to the poor performance of my company, wire-art studio. I can see that Jeremy has exactly the parts that I lack in running a company. Further, I know people in such culture are happy. Given these two strong motivation, I see no reason not to come. There are so much to be learned.

A record of my first photo at tangle-up AI

entry.title: Setting up ssh key
entry.content:
Create a public-private keypair instead of typing your password each time: On your local machine (linux/cygwin…):

ssh-keygen -t rsa
# I stick with the defaults there. Then copy the public key with
ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub user@server
entry.summary: How to setup ssh key for fast login

entry.title: Adding a grub entry
entry.content:
Add the below to /etc/grub.d/40_custom:

menuentry "Windows Boot Manager 2" {
    insmod part_gpt
    insmod fat
    set root=(hd1,gpt1)
    chainloader /EFI/Microsoft/Boot/ori_bootmgfw.efi
}

For the root thing… If it ain’t hd0,gpt1 or hd1,gpt1:

  • reboot to grub menue
  • press c
  • ls and you should see something like: (hd0), (hd1,gpt1) ....
  • you can ls (hd1,gpt1)/. If you see a $BOOT, thats the thing you should set
entry.summary: How to add a grub entry

entry.title: Dealing with Duo-booting when middle-fingered
entry.content:
Firstly, Microsoft is a piece of SHIT. I don’t know how, but they somehow was able to make the hardware to not detect the grub.efi DESPITE every configuration installing duo-boot ubuntu normally. The fix is to OVERWRITE THE WINDOWS EFI with grub.efi. Here is how you do it:

Step 1: Boot into Ubuntu through a USB stick
Step 2: In the terminal, mount the efi partition

sudo mount /dev/sda1 /mnt

The efi partition should have a structure similar to:

/mnt/EFI/
├── Boot/
│   └── bootx64.efi
├── Microsoft/
│   ├── Boot/
│   │   ├── bootmgfw.efi
│   │   ├── BCD
│   │   ├── memtest.efi
│   │   └── other boot-related files
├── Ubuntu/
|   ├── grubx64.efi

Step 3: rename the bootmgfw.efi to ori_bootmgfw.efi. Copy grubx64.efi to the directory and rename it as the original windows efi, bootmgfw.efi. Reboot the PC should boot into grub.

Note: bootmgfw.efi is the windows efi.

Finally, The computer should boot to grub when start. And FREED FROM THE CLUTCHES OF WINDOWS!!!!!!!
entry.summary: Describes a way to duo boot when the hardware refuses to boot into grub
